jordan: Hey — customer gave us a request_id `r_7a9b2f` and says their operation timed out. I tried a couple dashboard searches but not seeing anything. Fastest way to correlate request_id -> trace -> raw logs (console or CLI)?

maya: Start with the Requests page in Console: Observability -> Requests. Paste the request_id into the search box (use `request.id:r_7a9b2f`). That shows the request row with links to the trace and to raw logs (if we've retained them).

jordan: I did that but the console returned nothing. Any CLI fallback?

maya: Yep. Use the internal CLI `redwoodctl` to look up the request first — that bypasses some console UI filters. Example: 
```
redwoodctl requests lookup --id r_7a9b2f
```
That should print JSON with `trace_id` and `ingest_time`. If `trace_id` is present, you can query traces or logs by trace id.

sam: If lookup returns empty, check ingestion lag and sampling. Traces are sampled (default 1%) so some requests won't have a span. Logs should exist though unless log retention or log-routing flags removed. For logs: 
```
# query logs (service = api, last 15m)
redwoodctl logs query --service api --filter "request.id:r_7a9b2f" --from 15m
```
That searches structured logs. If you need raw pod logs because structured logs weren't routed, do `kubectl` against the pod that handled the request (use `redwoodctl requests lookup` to get `pod_name` if available).

jordan: What if `redwoodctl requests lookup` returns a `trace_id` but Jaeger/trace UI doesn't show spans?

maya: Could be sampling or delayed ingestion. Also check the trace index TTL. You can still search logs for `trace_id:` values. `redwoodctl logs query --filter "trace.id:<trace_id>" --from 30m` often finds the lines that reference the trace id even if the trace UI hasn't indexed it yet.

observability-bot: Tip: when you paste `request.id` into Console, set the time window to +/- 5m around the request's timestamp. Default UI window may be 1h which can hide short-lived requests. :mag:

sam: For debugging on a Live customer session, you can temporarily force-trace for a single request if you can reproduce: call our debug endpoint with header `X-Force-Trace: 1` or set `?debug_trace=1` (only enabled in non-prod/dedicated sandbox per policy).

jordan: Thanks — quick checklist I tried after reading this: 1) `redwoodctl requests lookup` -> got nothing. 2) `redwoodctl logs query --filter "request.id:r_7a9b2f"` -> nothing. 3) increased console window to 24h -> nothing.

maya: If both return nothing, ask support to check log-routing config for that org (sometimes customers disable structured logs). Also double-check the request id format — we have both `r_` and older `req-` prefixes.

sam: If you paste the request id here I can run a quick debug. If it's sensitive, DM me. Also include approximate client timestamp.

jordan: Pushed the id to you in DM, timestamp ~2025-06-11T16:03:20Z. Appreciate the assist! :pray:
